conceptTitle: She Got In His Car. The Seat Was Moved.

footage.loopStrategy: trim first 5 seconds taxi night city

onScreenHook:
She got in his car.
The passenger seat was moved.
She's 5'4". He's 6'2".
No one else has a key.
She drove home without a word.
caption:
She wasn't looking for anything.

She'd been in his car a hundred times. She grabbed her bag from the passenger seat and noticed the lever on the side.

It had been moved back. A lot.

She's 5'4". He's 6'2". She always moves the seat forward the moment she gets in. Always. It's automatic.

The seat was already moved forward — for someone shorter.

No one else has a key. No one had borrowed the car. She knew, because she would've known.

She got in the driver's seat. She adjusted the mirror. She drove home.

She said nothing.

She made dinner. She set the table. She asked about his day and he told her about a meeting and she nodded and passed the bread.

After he went to bed she sat in the kitchen for a long time trying to decide if she was imagining it.

She wasn't imagining it.

The worst part wasn't the discovery. It was the conversation she'd had with herself on the way home — the one where she talked herself in and out of trusting her own eyes.

If that kind of knowing-but-not-knowing keeps you awake at night, comment CALM.
